archetype.name: Dual-Threat (designed-run)
archetype.definition: A second-year first-rounder whose floor comes from his legs. He was among the most productive rushing quarterbacks in the league as a rookie, and he pairs that with an efficient, still-developing short-to-intermediate passing game.

report.headline: Two weeks of brilliant efficiency, then lost the job; now QB4 behind Winston and McCarthy.
report.take:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 is really one game. Against Dallas in Week 1 he went 23/29 for 230 yards and three touchdowns, added 54 rushing yards and piled up 21.9 passing EPA. In Week 2 at the Rams he played 12% of the snaps before leaving, and he did not practice in Week 3. Jameis Winston started the next four games, J.J. McCarthy started Week 7, and the depth chart now lists Dart as QB4. The season ranks that put him first among 45 qualifiers in EPA per dropback (0.578), completion rate and TD rate rest on 34 attempts. Most of those came against a Dallas defense that now ranks 30th by EPA.

There is still a real player in there. As a rookie he ran for 487 yards, third at the position, and posted 0.147 EPA per play, 19th of 63. That is a functional starter's line built partly on scrambles and designed runs. The small 2026 sample leans the right way on process, too. His time to throw dropped from 2.82 to 2.64 seconds, his bad-throw rate fell from 15% to 11.8%, and his aggressiveness rose from 13% to 17.24%. Quicker, cleaner and more willing to throw into windows is the developmental arc you want from a 23-year-old in year two, but 34 attempts can only hint at it.

The numbers hide how much finishing luck propped up the efficiency. He converted 8 of 9 third downs at an average of 6.7 yards to go and completed all 7 red-zone throws for three scores. Those rates have to come down. Isaiah Likely alone produced 12.2 EPA on nine targets. Dart also went 0-for-3 on throws of 20-plus air yards, and the rookie-year sack problem (36.5% of pressures turned into sacks, 43rd of 62) showed up again in a 33.3% pressure-to-sack rate, 28th of 38. Harbaugh's offense also runs far more than situations dictate: pass rate over expected is -8.4, 29th in the league. Even a healthy, starting Dart would be a lower-volume passer than his rookie 189 yards a game.

Where it heads depends entirely on the depth chart, not on the matchup. Three quarterbacks have started ahead of him since he got hurt. Until the team reverses course, his realistic weekly output is zero.

strengths.title: Designed runs that move the chains
strengths.body: His legs are the most established part of his game. He ranked 3rd among 63 quarterbacks in rushing yards as a rookie, and this year his six designed runs averaged 8.17 yards with a 100% success rate and no stuffs. The 2026 sample is tiny, but the trait carried over from 2025, so it is part of who he is rather than a blip.

strengths.title: Quicker, cleaner process in the pocket
strengths.body: Compared with his rookie year he got the ball out 0.18 seconds faster, cut his bad-throw rate by 3.2 points and threw into tight windows more often. Short throws were nearly automatic, at 92.9% completions with a 17.1 CPOE. This is the kind of second-year growth that usually holds, but it rests on 34 attempts, so treat it as a promising hint rather than proof.

strengths.title: Zero giveaways so far
strengths.body: He has thrown no interceptions and lost no fumbles in 2026, after averaging 0.42 interceptions per game as a rookie. One charted turnover-worthy fumble shows he isn't spotless, but his short-area accuracy keeps risk down.

concerns.title: Buried at QB4 after injury
concerns.body: This is the concern that overrides everything else. He left Week 2 after 12% of the snaps, sat out practice in Week 3, and has since watched Winston and then McCarthy start. That leaves no path to snaps unless the coaches change course.

concerns.title: Efficiency built on unrepeatable finishing
concerns.body: Most of his EPA came on third downs and in the red zone, at success rates of 88.9% and 100%. No quarterback sustains that. Much of it also came against a Dallas defense that now ranks 30th, so his true level is far closer to his rookie 0.147 EPA per play than to this year's league-best figure.

concerns.title: Sacks and the deep ball
concerns.body: He turned a third of his pressures into sacks, after ranking 43rd of 62 on the same measure as a rookie. That makes it a career-long trait rather than noise, partly the price of a quarterback who tries to extend plays. He also missed all three of his throws of 20-plus air yards, although the sample is too small to judge.

trend.note: He opened with a 26.6-point, 21.9-EPA win over Dallas. He then played only 12% of the snaps in Week 2 and hasn't appeared since, falling to fourth on the depth chart behind two different starters.

nextGame.headline: Soft Eagles pass defense, but QB4 won't see it
nextGame.body:
On paper Philadelphia is about as good a draw as a quarterback gets. The Eagles rank 27th in pass-defense EPA and dead last in both QB hit rate and sack rate, which would ease Dart's biggest flaw: taking sacks under pressure. They allow 19.5 PPR points a game to quarterbacks, 24th of 32. Their run defense ranks 31st by EPA, so a run-heavy Harbaugh plan with designed quarterback keepers would have room to work.

None of that reaches Dart unless the depth chart changes, and he sits behind both Winston and McCarthy. On the Eagles' side, edge rusher Nolan Smith Jr. and corner Michael Carter II were inactive last week, though their estimated return dates fall before this game. For the Giants, Skattebo's hamstring reportedly isn't serious. Theo Johnson is out, but he contributed -1.5 EPA on Dart's targets anyway. Mbow is a reserve tackle. The bye gives everyone 14 days of rest.

keyMatchups.title: No pass rush to fear
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia ranks last in both sack rate and hit rate. For a quarterback whose pressures turn into sacks a third of the time, that is the ideal opponent. It matters only if he takes the field.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends find room
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia allows 0.39 EPA per target to opposing lead tight ends, 25th in the league. Likely was Dart's most productive target by far, and that combination would be the pressure point.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Giants' Week 9 depth chart moves him off QB4; nothing else about this game matters for him.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is that Dart doesn't play meaningful snaps. Two veterans and a mid-season addition have started ahead of him since Week 2, and a 3-1 type stretch from those starters isn't required to keep him sidelined; simple continuity will do it. If injuries or a losing run push him back in, expect a player much closer to his rookie self than to his Week 1 line. He would bring real rushing value of around 25-40 yards a game, quicker and cleaner short passing, and a sack habit that persists, all inside a run-first offense that keeps passing volume low. In that scenario, figure 165-215 passing yards per game and EPA per dropback in a modestly positive 0.03-0.15 band. His perfect red-zone and third-down rates will regress hard.

What is sustainable is the rushing and the improved accuracy underneath. What is not is the league-best efficiency, the 8.8% TD rate and the zero-interception line.
swingFactors: Injury or benching of the quarterbacks ahead of him
Whether Harbaugh wants to evaluate his 2025 first-rounder late in the year
Health from whatever ended his Week 2

confidence.note: 34 attempts, one full game, and a role that now depends on decisions above him.
